title: The Shared Default Bucket
code:
def add(item, bucket=[]):
    bucket.append(item)
    return bucket

print(add(1))
print(add(2))
print(add(3, []))
print(add(4))
explanation:
Default values are evaluated **once**, when the `def` statement runs, not on every call. Every call that omits `bucket` gets the *same* list object, so it keeps growing: `[1]`, then `[1, 2]`.

`add(3, [])` passes its own fresh list, so it doesn't touch the shared default. `add(4)` goes back to the shared list: `[1, 2, 4]`.

The fix:
```
def add(item, bucket=None):
    if bucket is None:
        bucket = []
```
try_this: Print `add.__defaults__` after the calls. What do you see?

sources.title: Python FAQ: Why are default values shared between objects?
